subject: SIG: Clarify Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private responsibilities for Acme
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmepay.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: hosting mode responsibilities (Acme request)

Ben —

Thanks again for the SIG packet you sent last week. Our security team is running through the answers and has two items that need explicit callouts before we can close the review: one is the responsibility split for data processing and logging between Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes, and the second is network controls (ingress/egress points and where customer VPC peering is used).

Can you provide a concise mapping we can attach to our audit (1 page preferred) and any supporting artifacts you have (network diagram, SOC 2 evidence pointers, and the SIG doc with the hosted/dedicated/private rows filled)?

We're aiming to complete the review by EOD Friday (2028-06-23). If possible please copy your security lead on the reply.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Senior Security Analyst
Acme Payments Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmepay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting mode responsibilities (Acme request)

Hi Julia —

Appreciate the clear ask. High-level mapping below (I attached a filled SIG_answers_v1.pdf and a short network topology graphic). Jonas from security is cc'd and adds more technical detail in his note. If you prefer a single-page summary we can produce a PDF version with the three-row table called "Hosting Responsibility at a Glance" — happy to send that before EOD Thursday.

Summary (short):
- Hosted (Redwood Hosted API): Redwood manages model runtime, encryption at rest and in transit, multi-tenant tenancy with logical separation, and retains application logs in our controlled store. Customer data is processed in our hosted clusters; customers should not expect VPC peering in this mode. Recommended when rapid onboarding and no data residency requirements are primary.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools provisioned for your account. Redwood operationally manages the fleet, but compute and logs for your workload are isolated to your dedicated tenancy. Network: optional dedicated VPC peering or private link depending on region/provider; customer-configured egress controls recommended. Suitable where you need stronger isolation and predictable throughput but still want Redwood to run the control plane and ops.

- Private (VPC / On-prem): Full customer-managed compute (either in your VPC with an agent or on-prem package). Customer is responsible for host-level patching, instance-level keys, and physical access. Redwood operates a control plane endpoint optionally over an approved private network or not at all (air-gapped installs). This is the only mode that fully places processing and logs under customer infrastructure.

Attachments included: SIG_answers_v1.pdf (answers + ownership matrix), network_topology_acme.png (example: dedicated peering + optional private link). Jonas will add notes about log retention and encryption specifics.

Next steps:
1) I can send a one-page "Hosting Responsibility at a Glance" PDF by EOD Thursday.
2) Jonas will follow up with the SOC 2 crosswalk and where to find control evidence.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: SIG_answers_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 620KB), network_topology_acme.png (image/png, 240KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting mode responsibilities (Acme request)

Julia — quick technical addendum to Ben's overview:

1) Logging and retention
- Hosted: Application logs and inference metadata are retained in Redwood's managed stores. Default retention is configurable per-customer; we provide an account-level retention policy and can export logs to customer destinations (S3, BigQuery) via secure connectors. In the SIG matrix we flagged "Logging: Redwood-managed; export available" under Hosted.
- Dedicated: Logs are stored in account-isolated buckets/namespaces. We recommend using a dedicated export to your S3 for long-term retention/compliance.
- Private: All logging is done in-customer; no Redwood-managed copies unless explicitly configured.

2) Key management and encryption
- Hosted: Customer keys can be integrated via our KMS partner integrations (Bring Your Own Key). Data at rest in hosted clusters is encrypted.
- Dedicated: Support for KMS integration and customer-controlled envelope keys is standard. We can provide HSM-backed key wrapping options for Dedicated contracts.
- Private: Full customer control of keys. Redwood does not store keys in on-prem air-gapped deployments.

3) Network controls & peering
- Hosted: Public endpoints with TLS; IP allowlists for customer routes; no VPC peering.
- Dedicated: Optional VPC peering or cloud provider PrivateLink interconnects. When peering is used, traffic to model runtime is over private network segments; egress policies are configurable on the customer's side.
- Private: Runs within customer network; no public egress required.

4) SOC 2 / Evidence location
- SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we provide a redacted copy and an evidence crosswalk (folder link attached). For SIG fields that map to SOC 2 controls (CC1-CC8) we populate control IDs in the attached SIG_answers_v1.pdf under the column "Evidence (SOC 2 mapping)".

I've uploaded the SOC 2 crosswalk and the dedicated environment spec sheet (dedicated_specs_acme.xlsx) to our secure drive: https://redwood-drive.company/shared/acme/sig-evidence/

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call (security + infra) to walk through peering diagrams and export flows.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: dedicated_specs_acme.xlsx (spreadsheet, 150KB)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@acmepay.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting mode responsibilities (Acme request)

Ben / Jonas —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the artifacts. The Acme security and privacy teams reviewed the attached SIG_answers_v1.pdf and the SOC2 crosswalk Jon linked. A couple quick confirmations before we close:

- For Dedicated: we want dedicated VPC peering plus log export to our S3; you'll confirm peering availability in us-west-2 and provide the peering checklist.
- For Private/on-prem: noted that customer is responsible for host patching — accepted.

Assuming peering availability in us-west-2 and the checklist, we can mark the SIG as satisfied and move forward with the Dedicated pilot. Please send the peering checklist and I'll route to our infra team.

Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure Security
Acme Payments Inc.
